notes: Official ACIAR page verified live at https://www.aciar.gov.au/scholarships/john-allwright-fellowship (rendered in a browser; direct webfetch returned HTTP 403 but the page itself is readable and complete). The John Allwright Fellowship is an Australian Government (ACIAR) merit-based scheme: 'It provides Masters by Research or PhD scholarships to agricultural researchers, administered through the Australia Awards system.' Fellows are nominated out of ACIAR research projects and then study at an Australian tertiary institution of their choosing; no university, department or supervising professor is attached to the scholarship itself, and the word 'supervisor' does not appear anywhere on the official page. Per batch rules this is a national/government scheme with no attached institution -> not_applicable. Official contact details on the page are administrative only (ACIAR, 38 Sydney Ave, Forrest ACT 2603, phone 61 2 6217 0500).

Official Griffith University page verified live and readable at https://www.griffith.edu.au/international/scholarships-finance/scholarships/vice-chancellors-international-scholarship. This is a university-wide, competitive 50% coursework tuition-fee waiver for commencing international undergraduate and postgraduate coursework students; selection is by 'a University panel' on GPA, offer of place, academic records and a personal statement, and the page explicitly excludes 'students enrolling in Higher Degree Research'. No faculty supervisor, research group or named academic is attached to the award; the only contact route is the administrative 'Enquire' link (https://www.griffith.edu.au/international/contact-us). Because no faculty tie exists on any official Griffith page, no supervisor could be verified without inventing one.

Official Griffith University page verified live and readable at https://www.griffith.edu.au/international/scholarships-finance/scholarships/international-academic-merit-scholarship. This is an automatic 20% coursework tuition-fee reduction ('You don't need to apply for the scholarship... Just apply to study at Griffith and we will let you know if you are successful') for international undergraduate and postgraduate coursework students, assessed purely on prior GPA and entry requirements, with an explicit exclusion of Higher Degree Research enrolment. No faculty supervisor, programme director or research group is attached to the award; the page's only contact route is the administrative 'Enquire' link (https://www.griffith.edu.au/international/contact-us). No supervised-research component exists, so no professor could be tied to this scholarship from official Griffith sources.

Official Immigration New Zealand (MBIE) page verified live and readable at https://www.immigration.govt.nz/about-us/our-strategies-and-programmes/supporting-refugees-and-asylum-seekers/new-zealand-refugee-health-scholarship-programme, together with the administering body's page at https://www.universitiesnz.ac.nz/scholarships/new-zealand-refugee-health-scholarship. The programme was 'developed in 2025 by the National Leadership and Coordination Service (NLCS), a joint function established through a partnership between the Ministry of Business Innovation and Employment (MBIE) | Immigration New Zealand, the Ministry of Health, and the Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora'. It is a government-partnership scheme; recipients 'commence or complete their undergraduate, post-graduate or other health-related education and training' at any 'NZQA-accredited tertiary provider' of their own choosing, and applications are lodged through the Universities New Zealand Community Force portal. No institution, department or supervising professor is attached to the scholarship itself - the only published contacts are administrative (nzrefugeehealthscholarships@mbie.govt.nz and scholarships-cf@universitiesnz.ac.nz). Per batch rules, a national/government scheme with no attached institution -> not_applicable.
